summary: Make the Tier-1 own-cookie unlock discoverable: rewrite narrative.auth_narrative so the generated Authentication / Auth Setup sections name all three session routes, the browser extraction steps, the MCP route, the safety posture and the honest-failure behaviour; add an OPTIONAL substack_session user_config (+ server.env) to manifest.json so the MCPB bundle prompts for the cookie.
reason: The shipped Tier-1 capability (substack-tier1-session-cookie) was undiscoverable from the docs. The whole Authentication section was one sentence — 'provide your own Substack session cookie (substack.sid)' — which named no route, gave no browser instructions and never mentioned the MCP path, so a reader who subscribes to a paid post could not learn from the documentation how to unlock it. The prose is GENERATED from .manuscripts/<run>/research.json at narrative.auth_narrative, so the correction had to land there rather than in README.md/SKILL.md, which are re-synced by dogfood (the same trap that silently reverted Snipd's 2026-07-14 hand-fix for six weeks). The rewritten narrative documents the precedence chain AS IMPLEMENTED in internal/substack/session.go: SUBSTACK_SESSION, then SUBSTACK_COOKIE_FILE (authoritative once set — a missing/unparseable/sid-less explicit file is a hard error), then the default <config-dir>/cookie.json (best-effort, degrades to anonymous with a warning). NOTE: this supersedes the stale precedence prose in substack-tier1-session-cookie.json's reason field and in the EnvCookieFile const comment (session.go), both of which describe the config-dir file as ranking ABOVE SUBSTACK_COOKIE_FILE; the code and a live probe both say otherwise. manifest.json's user_config addition follows the published medium-reader precedent (auth_type none, yet an optional sensitive medium_session user_config) — it is what makes the Claude Desktop bundle prompt for the cookie; it is hand-added to a generated artefact and must be re-applied on any reprint. Out of scope and deliberately NOT attempted, all requiring a reprint or code change: spec.yaml's auth.type none (the structural root of the missing env-var row and the missing user_config), doctor's misleading 'OK Auth: not required' line, and an auth subcommand.
validated_outcome: Acceptance-tested against the INSTALLED published binary (~/.local/bin/substack-reader-pp-cli, 2026.8.2) on 2026-09-10, each route from a clean empty home via SUBSTACK_READER_HOME pointed at a temp dir, on the paid post uxmentor/the-work-you-keep-calling-untangling (wordcount 2237): no cookie anywhere -> access preview, authenticated false, full false, 589 words; SUBSTACK_SESSION as a bare sid -> access entitled, authenticated true, full true; SUBSTACK_SESSION as a 'substack.sid=<value>' fragment -> entitled; {"substack.sid":"s%3A..."} at <config-dir>/cookie.json with no env set -> entitled; SUBSTACK_COOKIE_FILE pointing at that file elsewhere on disk -> entitled. Precedence probe: a valid SUBSTACK_COOKIE_FILE alongside a garbage config-dir cookie.json -> entitled, confirming SUBSTACK_COOKIE_FILE outranks the default file. Doc fidelity: cli-printing-press 4.31.2 dogfood re-synced README.md/SKILL.md from the corrected research.json, and a second dogfood run was a byte-for-byte no-op on both files (diff clean), so the committed prose is exactly what generation produces. KNOWN REGRESSION RE-CONFIRMED: that doc-sync also re-derives SKILL.md's post-auth line as 'substack-pp-cli doctor' (the wrong binary) — upstream bug F6, which STATUS.md recorded as 'fixed at source' but which in fact re-breaks on every dogfood run; corrected back to substack-reader-pp-cli by hand here and NOT propagated to the published tree. go build ./... and go vet ./... green. Section ownership probed empirically: the doc-sync rewrites only the sections it owns (Authentication / Auth Setup), so the hand-added session env-var table under 'Paths & environment variables' and the optional SUBSTACK_SESSION env example in the Claude Desktop config block both survived a subsequent dogfood run byte-for-byte — which is why those two are hand-edited rather than sourced from research.json. Greptile review on PR #1974 found two real defects in the first draft of this prose, both fixed at the research.json source and re-verified: (P1) the documented config-dir cookie route did not work on a clean install — the config directory does not exist after installation and no command creates it (doctor leaves it absent), so the documented redirect exited 1; the snippet now creates it 0700 first, and following the corrected lines literally on a clean home returns access entitled. The first acceptance pass had masked this by creating the directory outside the documented steps — a reminder that 'follow your own instructions literally' means literally. (P2) the warning behaviour was overstated: probing all four states of the default cookie file against the installed binary gives absent -> silent, empty -> warns (unparseable JSON), {} -> silent, corrupt -> warns, so only an existing-but-unreadable/unparseable file warns; the sentence now draws the line at read/parse failure. All six PR checks pass (Verify, Govulncheck, Validate SKILL.md against shipped CLI source, Validate MCPB manifest contract, Greptile Review, Greptile policy gate). Reprint 2026-10-28 (press 4.34.2): the fresh README dropped both hand-additions (the Claude Desktop env example and the Session environment variables table); both were restored by hand at the equivalent places (after the manual JSON config, and after the new Local data section). The Authentication prose regenerated from narrative.auth_narrative unchanged. They will drop again at every reprint until they are sourced from research.json.
